blocks.instruction: Fill in the gaps with the correct answer. ( 6 x 1 = 6 )

items.label: c.

items.answer: True

blocks.instruction: Write a short note on the following. ( 2 x 2 = 4 )

items.label: a.
items.q: Importance of water in our diet.
items.answer: Water is an important part of our diet. It helps in digesting food, keeps our skin and body healthy, and removes waste from the body through urine, sweat and faeces. Water-rich fruits like watermelon and cucumber also help keep water in the body.

answerPoints.point: Water helps digest food / keeps skin and body healthy
Water removes waste from the body (urine, sweat, faeces); drink enough water / eat water-rich fruits

rubric.descriptor: Two correct points about why water is needed (digestion, healthy skin/body, removing waste, keeping the body cool or hydrated).
One correct point.
No correct point.

items.modelAnswer: Water helps us digest food and keeps our skin and body healthy. It removes waste from our body through urine and sweat, so we should drink enough water every day.

items.label: b.
items.q: Balanced food
items.answer: Balanced food has food from all three food groups in the right quantities: protective foods (fruits and vegetables) the most, then body-building foods, and some energy-giving foods. It keeps us healthy, active and happy.

answerPoints.point: Contains all three food groups (energy-giving, body-building, protective) in the right amounts
Keeps us healthy, active and happy / gives everything the body needs (examples welcome)

rubric.descriptor: Says balanced food has all the food groups in the right amounts AND why it is good for us.
Only one of these, or a list of healthy foods without the idea of all food groups.
Nothing correct.

items.modelAnswer: Balanced food has energy-giving, body-building and protective foods in the right amounts, with more fruits and vegetables. It keeps us healthy, active and happy.

sections.title: Section – B : IDENTIFICATION AND CLASSIFICATION ( 12 marks )
sections.heading: Section – B : IDENTIFICATION AND CLASSIFICATION ( 12 marks )

items.label: a.
items.q: What did Surabhi’s grandmother use to eat to during summers and winters?
items.answer: She used to eat jau (barley) roti during summers and jowar and bajra roti in winters.
acceptable: jau roti in summers, jowar and bajra roti in winters
barley roti in summer, jowar and bajra roti in winter
jowar bajra roti in winter and jau roti in summer

rubric.descriptor: Summers: jau (barley) roti AND winters: jowar and/or bajra roti (millet rotis).
Only one season correct, or just "millet rotis" without the seasons.
No correct food.

items.modelAnswer: In summers she ate jau roti, and in winters she ate jowar and bajra roti.
items.teacherNote: Printed as "use to eat to" (stray "to"; means "used to eat") and "Surabhi" (the textbook spells it "Surbhi"). Kept as printed. Answers that spell the name either way (Surabhi / Surbhi) are fully correct.

items.label: b.
items.q: Why do you think we should avoid eating junk food?
items.answer: Junk food has high amounts of oil, salt and sugar, so eating it regularly and in large quantities is not healthy for us.

rubric.descriptor: A sensible reason: too much oil, salt or sugar; makes us unhealthy, fat or ill; has little nutrition.
A vague reason ("it is bad") with no explanation.
No sensible reason.

items.modelAnswer: Junk food has too much oil, salt and sugar, so it is not good for our health.

items.label: c.
items.q: Why do we need to eat different kinds of food items?
items.answer: No single food contains all the nutrients our body needs, so we must eat a variety of foods to stay healthy, energetic and strong.

rubric.descriptor: Says no single food has all the nutrients / we need energy, body-building and protection, so we eat many kinds of food.
Says only "to stay healthy" without the reason.
No sensible reason.

items.modelAnswer: No single food has all the nutrients our body needs, so we eat different foods to stay healthy and strong.

items.label: d.
items.q: How is solar cooker useful to us?
items.answer: A solar cooker cooks food using sunlight instead of gas or electricity, and it does not pollute the environment with smoke or ash.

rubric.descriptor: Cooks food with sunlight (saves gas/fuel/electricity) AND/OR causes no smoke or pollution.
Says only "it cooks food" without mentioning sunlight or no pollution.
No sensible answer.

items.modelAnswer: It cooks food with sunlight, so it saves gas and does not make smoke or ash.

items.label: e.
items.q: Who is a ‘Chef’?
items.answer: A chef is a professional cook who is skilled in all aspects of food preparation. In French, ‘chef’ means the head of the kitchen.

rubric.descriptor: A professional / trained / skilled cook, or the head of a kitchen.
Says only "a person who cooks" (any cook at home).
No sensible answer.

items.modelAnswer: A chef is a professional cook who is skilled in preparing food.

blocks.adaptation: The printed table has one column for each food type; each column is asked separately here.

items.q: Protective Foods
items.answer: Protective foods help us fight against diseases and protect us from them. Examples: fruits and vegetables like carrot, orange, papaya, spinach, guava, amla, tomato.

rubric.descriptor: Says they protect us from / help us fight diseases (an example is welcome).
Gives only examples of protective foods, with no description.
Wrong or no description.

items.modelAnswer: They protect us from diseases, e.g. carrot, orange, spinach.
items.markingGuide: 1 mark for the protective-foods column. Accept the job (protect from diseases) with or without examples; examples alone get ½.
items.teacherNote: Printed "( 2 x 1 = 2 )" for a two-column table with one empty row. Read as 1 mark per column (describe each food type). A child who writes the difference as a pair of contrasting sentences also gets full marks.

items.q: Energy Giving Foods
items.answer: Energy-giving foods give our body energy to work and play. Examples: rice, wheat, potato, maize, banana, sweet potato, honey, millets, butter, ghee, oil.

rubric.descriptor: Says they give us energy (an example is welcome).
Gives only examples of energy-giving foods, with no description.
Wrong or no description.

items.modelAnswer: They give us energy to work and play, e.g. rice, wheat, potato.
items.markingGuide: 1 mark for the energy-giving-foods column. Accept the job (give energy) with or without examples; examples alone get ½.
items.teacherNote: Printed "( 2 x 1 = 2 )" for a two-column table with one empty row. Read as 1 mark per column (describe each food type).

blocks.instruction: Give an example of the ingredients or food items that match each of the tastes listed below? ( 6 x ½ = 3 )
blocks.adaptation: Each taste in the printed table is asked separately here; write one food for each.

items.q: Sweet
items.answer: Jaggery
items.markingGuide: Any one food or ingredient that tastes sweet: ½ mark.

items.q: Sour
items.answer: Tamarind
items.markingGuide: Any one food or ingredient that tastes sour: ½ mark.

items.q: Salty
items.answer: Salt
items.markingGuide: Any one food or ingredient that tastes salty: ½ mark.

items.q: Pungent
items.answer: Green chilli
items.markingGuide: Any one food or ingredient that tastes pungent (hot / spicy, teekha): ½ mark.

items.q: Bitter
items.answer: Neem
items.markingGuide: Any one food or ingredient that tastes bitter (karva): ½ mark.

items.q: Astringent
items.answer: Raw mango
items.markingGuide: Any one food or ingredient that tastes astringent (kasaila: dries the mouth, like raw banana or amla): ½ mark.
items.teacherNote: Astringent (kasaila) is the least familiar taste; foods are classed differently in different homes and regions, so accept any sensible example.

blocks.instruction: Draw any two junk food and also write the names. ( 2 x 1 = 2 )
blocks.adaptation: Do this on the printed sheet (one junk food in each box, with its name on the line); your parent marks it.

items.q: Draw any two junk food and also write the names.
items.label: Box 1
items.answer: A recognisable drawing of one junk food with its name, e.g. burger, pizza, chips, soft drink, bread pakoda, noodles, French fries, packaged snacks.
items.markingGuide: Box 1: ½ for a recognisable drawing of a junk food, ½ for writing its correct name. Junk food = food high in oil, salt or sugar (textbook: soft drinks, chips, bread pakoda, burgers, pizza, over-processed packaged food).

rubric.descriptor: A junk food drawn recognisably AND correctly named.
Drawing or name only, or a healthy food drawn.
Nothing drawn or named, or both wrong.

items.modelAnswer: A drawing of a burger, named "Burger".

items.q: Draw any two junk food and also write the names.
items.label: Box 2
items.answer: A recognisable drawing of a second, different junk food with its name, e.g. pizza, chips, soft drink, bread pakoda, noodles, French fries, packaged snacks.
items.markingGuide: Box 2: ½ for a recognisable drawing of a different junk food from Box 1, ½ for its correct name.

rubric.descriptor: A second, different junk food drawn recognisably AND correctly named.
Drawing or name only, a repeat of Box 1, or a healthy food drawn.
Nothing drawn or named, or both wrong.

items.modelAnswer: A drawing of a packet of chips, named "Chips".
items.teacherNote: The paper prints two boxes, each with a name line, for "( 2 x 1 = 2 )": 1 mark per box (½ drawing + ½ name). Grammar "two junk food" kept as printed.

sections.title: Section – C :  DISCOVERY OF FACTS ( 13 marks )
sections.heading: Section – C :  DISCOVERY OF FACTS ( 13 marks )

items.label: a.
items.q: Food items which can be eaten without cooking ______ ______
items.answer: Any two of: fruit chaat, vegetable salad, fruits, raw vegetables, sprouts, nuts, curd
items.markingGuide: Any one correct example: ½ mark; two different correct examples: 1 mark.

items.label: b.
items.q: Water – rich fruits ______ ______
items.answer: Any two of: watermelon, cucumber, orange, muskmelon, grapes, pineapple
items.markingGuide: Any one correct example: ½ mark; two different correct examples: 1 mark. The textbook names watermelon and cucumber; any juicy fruit is fine.
items.teacherNote: Printed "Water – rich" with a spaced dash; kept. Cucumber (named in the textbook) is accepted although many children call it a vegetable.

items.label: c.
items.q: Food groups ______ ______
items.answer: Any two of: energy-giving foods, body-building foods, protective foods
items.markingGuide: Any one correct example: ½ mark; two different correct examples: 1 mark. Textbook groups: energy-giving, body-building, protective. A child who names nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins) may be given credit at the parent's judgement.

items.label: d.
items.q: Food items in the stall of super food ______ ______
items.answer: Any two of: jowar upma, jowar roti, bajra roti, jau roti, ragi laddu, bajre-ki-khichdi (millet foods)
items.markingGuide: Any one correct example: ½ mark; two different correct examples: 1 mark. The "super food" stall in the textbook sold millet foods (jowar upma; Surbhi recalls jowar, bajra and jau rotis). Any millet or millet dish is fine.

items.label: e.
items.q: Meals of the day ______ ______
items.answer: Any two of: breakfast, lunch, dinner
items.markingGuide: Any one correct example: ½ mark; two different correct examples: 1 mark.

items.q: Match the following.
items.answer: a. Boiling – rice; b. Steaming – idiyappam; c. Frying – puri; d. Roasting – popcorn; e. Grilling – chicken; f. Baking – cakes.

rubric.descriptor: All six pairs correct (Roasting/Grilling may be popcorn/chicken either way).
Some pairs correct: ½ mark for each correct pair.
No pair correct.

items.teacherNote: Popcorn and chicken can each be cooked by roasting or grilling, so Roasting – chicken with Grilling – popcorn is also accepted. The printed mark bracket "( 6 x ½ = 3)" has no space before ")"; kept.

blocks.instruction: Locate the following states in the given map. ( 3 x 1 = 3 )
blocks.adaptation: Do this on the printed sheet: mark and name each state on the map; your parent marks it with the answer map.

stimulus.caption: Outline map of India with state boundaries (no names).
stimulus.alt: Outline political map of India showing state borders without any names.

items.label: a.
items.q: Andhra Pradesh
items.answer: Andhra Pradesh marked correctly on the map (south-east coast, on the Bay of Bengal).
items.markingGuide: Answer map: orange. Andhra Pradesh: the long state on the south-east coast along the Bay of Bengal, south of Odisha, east of Karnataka and north of Tamil Nadu; it lies south and east of Telangana. 1 mark if the right region is marked and named; ½ if it is marked in the right area but overlaps a neighbour.

rubric.descriptor: The correct state is marked and named.
Marked near the right place but spilling into a neighbouring state, or marked without a name.
Wrong state or not marked.

items.modelAnswer: The coastal state on the south-east side of India is shaded and named Andhra Pradesh.
items.teacherNote: Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telangana are the states where Ugadi Pachadi is a traditional food (textbook spelling "Telengana"). The answer map shades all three.

items.label: b.
items.q: Karnataka
items.answer: Karnataka marked correctly on the map (south-west, on the Arabian Sea coast).
items.markingGuide: Answer map: green. Karnataka: in the south-west, on the Arabian Sea coast south of Goa and Maharashtra, north of Kerala, west of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. 1 mark if the right region is marked and named; ½ if it is marked in the right area but overlaps a neighbour.

rubric.descriptor: The correct state is marked and named.
Marked near the right place but spilling into a neighbouring state, or marked without a name.
Wrong state or not marked.

items.modelAnswer: The state on the south-west coast above Kerala is shaded and named Karnataka.

items.label: c.
items.q: Telangana
items.answer: Telangana marked correctly on the map (inland, north-west of Andhra Pradesh).
items.markingGuide: Answer map: red. Telangana: an inland state (no coast) in the Deccan, south of Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh, north-west of Andhra Pradesh and north-east of Karnataka. 1 mark if the right region is marked and named; ½ if it is marked in the right area but overlaps a neighbour.

rubric.descriptor: The correct state is marked and named.
Marked near the right place but spilling into a neighbouring state, or marked without a name.
Wrong state or not marked.

items.modelAnswer: The inland state north-west of Andhra Pradesh is shaded and named Telangana.
